rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results sections <U+2014> authors report their own laboratory filtration experiments with a scaled PMMA media filter, two recycled-glass media, six filtration cycles with reclaimed wastewater, measuring retained solids per layer and OCT fouling coverage (Table 3, Fig. 5).
rows.notes: The study is a laboratory methodology paper on using optical coherence tomography to quantify particle retention across depth in pressurised media filters used in drip irrigation with reclaimed wastewater. It contains no crop, yield, crop-type or climate/environmental data and no measurement of drip irrigation effectiveness on crop production; the cited claim that drip effectiveness varies with crop type and environmental conditions is not addressed in any way. The study shows only that OCT pixel coverage correlates with laboratory-determined retained solids in filter media (R2 0.65 overall) and that most retention occurs in the top 20 mm of the bed. This is a filtration-maintenance topic, not a crop-production effect of drip, so Q2 is no; it is not an upstream precondition of the claimed yield effect either.

notes: Full text appears complete (introduction through conclusions); tables and figures are referenced but their contents are not reproduced. The study is misattributed by the review: it concerns media filter fouling assessment, not drip irrigation effects on crop yields.
